page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores with hyper-threading, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The system is equipped with 512 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8 GB per vCPU.

This instance includes 2400 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, offering high-speed local data access. It is optimized for network and EBS performance, delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 75 Gbps. This combination of high-speed local storage and high network throughput supports data-intensive operations.

In benchmark testing, the r5dn.16xlarge demonstrates strong memory bandwidth performance, scoring in the top tier for both large-block read and write operations. Its CPU performance is average overall, with strong results in extended instruction tests, though single-core performance and single-threaded compression tasks fall into the lower tier. Multi-core processing, database operations, and web serving throughput remain consistently in the average range.

Given its high memory density, integrated NVMe storage, and substantial network bandwidth, this instance offers a balanced cost-to-resource profile for memory-bound workloads that do not require GPU acceleration. It is highly suited for large-scale databases, in-memory caching, big data analytics, and enterprise applications requiring high throughput and low-latency storage access.
